question: What is the main goal of taking a dietary supplement?

options.A: To completely replace regular hospital meals
options.B: To add extra nutrients to a person's diet
options.C: To cure chronic infectious diseases overnight
options.D: To serve as the main source of daily calories

explanation: Supplements are simply meant to top up the nutrients you might be missing from your regular meals. You've got this! [learn more](GNS227_U7_T014#GNS227_U7_T014_h1)

question: Why shouldn't dietary supplements replace whole foods?

options.A: Supplements are always too expensive for ordinary patients to afford daily
options.B: Whole foods provide a complex balance of nutrients and fiber that isolated supplements lack
options.C: Conventional foods contain prescription drugs that supplements completely lack
options.D: The human digestive tract cannot absorb any chemical compound created in a laboratory

explanation: Real foods give you a rich mix of fiber and interacting nutrients that a single pill just can't copy. Balance is key! [learn more](GNS227_U7_T014#GNS227_U7_T014_h1)

question: Which agency is responsible for regulating food and dietary supplements in Nigeria?
explanation: NAFDAC is our local body that keeps us safe by regulating drugs, food, and supplements in Nigeria. Great to keep in mind for clinical practice! [learn more](GNS227_U7_T014#GNS227_U7_T014_h2)

question: What is the safest action for a nurse when a patient brings an unregistered herbal supplement to the ward?

options.A: Store the product in the nurse's station and prescribe it to other patients
options.B: Encourage the patient to double the normal dosage for faster healing results
options.C: Taste the liquid content first to verify if it contains real medicinal herbs
options.D: Advise the patient to avoid using it because safety and quality cannot be guaranteed

explanation: If it's unregistered, we can't vouch for its safety or purity. Always advise caution with unknown products! [learn more](GNS227_U7_T014#GNS227_U7_T014_h2)

question: Under which category of supplements is iron classified?
explanation: Iron is a vital mineral our bodies need to build hemoglobin for red blood cells. Simple and classic nursing knowledge! [learn more](GNS227_U7_T014#GNS227_U7_T014_h3)

question: Why do people commonly take protein powder supplements?

options.A: To treat acute bacterial infections in the respiratory tract
options.B: To support muscle growth and repair after physical exercise
options.C: To permanently lower high blood pressure levels
options.D: To cure chronic iron-deficiency anemia quickly

explanation: Protein gives the body the building blocks (amino acids) it needs to repair and build up muscle tissue after a workout. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T014#GNS227_U7_T014_h3)

question: Which supplement is very important during early pregnancy to prevent neural tube defects?
explanation: Folic acid is a prenatal superstar! It protects the baby's developing brain and spine in the early weeks. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T014#GNS227_U7_T014_h4)

question: Why should a nurse check lab results before encouraging a patient to take high-dose supplements?

options.A: To find out if the patient is allergic to plastic medicine bottles
options.B: To make sure the patient can afford the expensive brand names sold in pharmacies
options.C: To calculate the exact hospital bed tax for nutritional therapy
options.D: To confirm the specific nutrient deficiency rather than guessing based on general fatigue

explanation: We test to be sure what's actually lacking. Guessing can lead to wasting money or even vitamin toxicity! [learn more](GNS227_U7_T014#GNS227_U7_T014_h4)

question: Which type of vitamin is most likely to cause toxicity if taken in excess because they store up in body fat?
explanation: Vitamins A, D, E, and K dissolve in fat and hang around in the body instead of being flushed out in urine. Too much of a good thing can be harmful! [learn more](GNS227_U7_T014#GNS227_U7_T014_h5)

question: A patient on warfarin for a heart condition starts taking a daily garlic supplement. What is the major concern here?

options.A: The combination can significantly increase the risk of bleeding
options.B: The warfarin will turn the garlic tablets into poison
options.C: The patient will develop severe vitamin C toxicity
options.D: The garlic will completely cure the heart condition overnight

explanation: Garlic naturally thins the blood a little. Combined with warfarin, it can dangerously boost the bleeding risk. Always screen for herbal-drug interactions! [learn more](GNS227_U7_T014#GNS227_U7_T014_h5)

question: Why do many patients forget to mention their herbal supplements during a medication history interview?

options.A: Herbal products dissolve instantly and leave no trace in the body
options.B: Hospital regulations strictly forbid talking about traditional medicine
options.C: Nurses never ask about home remedies during admission
options.D: They consider supplements to be harmless food items rather than real drugs

explanation: Patients often view herbs as 'just food' or natural, so it doesn't cross their minds to report them as medications. That's why we always have to ask! [learn more](GNS227_U7_T014#GNS227_U7_T014_h6)

question: When assessing a patient's supplement use, which detail is MOST important to record?

options.A: The color and shape of the retail cardboard packaging
options.B: The political affiliation of the supplement manufacturer
options.C: The exact product name, dosage, and frequency of intake
options.D: The name of the transport vehicle used to deliver the pills

explanation: Knowing the exact name and dose helps you and the medical team spot potential drug clashes right away. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T014#GNS227_U7_T014_h6)

question: How should a nurse respond to a patient who admits to using traditional herbal remedies?

options.A: By threatening to discharge the patient immediately from the hospital
options.B: By prescribing synthetic antibiotics to replace the herbal mixture
options.C: With an open, non-judgmental attitude to encourage honest communication
options.D: By laughing at the remedies to show they have no scientific value

explanation: Keeping a welcoming, non-judgmental vibe makes patients trust us enough to share everything they're taking. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T014#GNS227_U7_T014_h7)

question: Which of these is NOT a good topic for patient education regarding dietary supplements?

options.A: Bringing all supplement containers to clinic appointments for review
options.B: Checking for valid NAFDAC registration numbers on product labels
options.C: How to manufacture herbal capsules at home in your kitchen
options.D: Reporting unusual side effects or symptoms to a healthcare provider

explanation: As nurses, we teach safety, checking labels, and reporting side effects—we definitely don't encourage brewing or making DIY pills at home! [learn more](GNS227_U7_T014#GNS227_U7_T014_h7)
